pypi.summary: The subset of a Qt installation needed by PyQt6.

earlier.note: Qt's libraries: the network imports are QtNetwork / QtBluetooth / FFmpeg's streaming (SAP multicast 224.2.127.254), the process imports QtCore's QProcess and QtTest; prctl names threads. The one YARA hit ('suspicious_network_tools' in libQt6Quick3DParticles) matches bytes of compressed data, no command. No attestation: content review only.

reviewed.note: macOS arm64 and Windows amd64 wheels of the reviewed Qt build: Qt frameworks / DLLs in place of the .so files; added only the platform's QML styles (macOS, iOS, Windows, NativeStyle), Info.plist/PrivacyInfo, macOS's static permission plugins (.a/.o) and FFmpeg/Mesa DLLs; every other QML file is identical (Windows CRLF only), qmldir adds the platform style. Network imports are QtNetwork and FFmpeg (as on Linux, SAP multicast 224.2.127.254), process ones QProcess/QDesktopServices and Qt3D's renderer (as on Linux); qwindows: BitBlt (screen grab API), a debugger check like xcb's -nograb; opengl32sw is Mesa llvmpipe (its window hook is WGL's). The YARA hit in Qt6Quick3DParticles.dll is the reviewed 'Nc' byte match in compressed data. The macOS SQL driver plugins link build-host paths (Postgres.app, Homebrew libiodbc, /usr/local libmimerapi), loaded only if such a driver is opened. No .pth, no hook, no executables. No attestation: content review only.
